findings.title: Convert cents to dollars in the legacy estimate handler
findings.comment: `baseRateFor` now returns cents, but `quickEstimate` in `api.ts` still passes its result to `roundDollars(...).toFixed(2)`, which treats it as dollars. Every marketing-widget estimate is therefore 100 times too high: a domestic 0.5 kg parcel renders `310.00` next to the dollar sign while `handleQuote` returns $3.10. Update that caller to use `centsToDollars` before formatting.

findings.title: Restore positive, finite weight validation before pricing
findings.comment: The old `quoteShipment` guard was removed, while `parseQuoteRequest` still checks only that the weight has type `number`. Consequently, `handleQuote` now returns 200 for zero and negative weights instead of the documented 400; a domestic weight of -10 even produces a zero-dollar total with a negative subtotal. Non-finite numeric inputs also produce successful replies containing non-finite prices. Restore the validation at the API boundary, or retain the guard together with the handler's former RangeError-to-400 conversion.

findings.title: Preserve inclusive upper bounds when selecting weight tiers
findings.comment: Using `<` instead of the previous `<=` sends parcels weighing exactly 1, 5, or 20 kg into the next tier, contrary to both the `WeightTier` contract and README. For example, a domestic 1 kg parcel now costs $4.95 instead of $3.70, and a 5 kg parcel costs $11.50 instead of $8.75. Restore the inclusive comparison so the cents conversion does not change boundary pricing.
